finding: The 16/45 missed clear-cross/grid centers in the previously frozen broad synthetic validation are the outer perimeter nodes of its spacing-9 grid. That fixture extends each grid line by integer spacing/2 = 4 pixels beyond its outer node. The provider requires at least 5 foreground pixels in both directions for each of two opposing line pairs, so these perimeter nodes are ineligible before marker-conflict or NMS checks. The measured marker-like probability at grid centers and across each 5x5 mask footprint was zero.

limitations: These are small generated Gray8 component cases using a fixed oracle plot polygon, empty OCR, and no trained model. They do not measure production calibration or real graph quality.
Synthetic validation here diagnoses a rule boundary; it is not candidate validation, release acceptance, or sealed acceptance.

The center annotation labels every generated lattice node, including perimeter nodes whose line continuation is shorter than the provider's minimum-arm contract. This is why the prior broad score counts 16 nodes as missed even though the current rule intentionally rejects them.
No real-development cases were examined, so whether real graphs need four-pixel edge-junction support remains unknown.
